tabs.$description: Two visual styles per the user's own reference screenshots — segmented (a pill track, the active tab raised on a white pill) and underline (plain text, active tab marked by a blue bottom bar). Both share the same size grid and content variants (text-only, +icon-left, +counter, +icon+counter, icon-only). No hard cap on tab count is enforced by the component — that's a content decision, not a token; the tab list scrolls horizontally (overflow-x: auto) if it doesn't fit, and the docs page carries a practical (5-7 comfortable) guideline rather than a hard-coded number.

item.$description: Text stays 14px (size.base) at both sm and base — unlike button/input where type scales with the control size, here only icon size / padding / counter size scale; the label size is flat, per spec.

label.$description: Base (inactive) weight. Active state overrides fontWeight to weight.semibold only — same size/family/leading, see state.*.active.fontWeight in each style below.

counter.$description: Reuses component.counter.onNeutral exactly as built for the secondary button — inactive tab pairs with onNeutral.inactive (quiet gray.300 bg, dark label), active tab pairs with onNeutral.active (inverts to fill.primary blue, white label). Repurposes the same visual distinction (quiet vs. pops-blue) for tab-selection state instead of notification-freshness state — the tokens don't encode 'why', only how it looks, so this reuse is legitimate rather than a semantic stretch. No new counter tokens needed; sized via component.counter.size (sm/base, same keys).

segmented.$description: A track (surface.sunken — literally the same 'recessed' token as an input's own background) holding the tabs; the active tab sits on a raised white pill (surface.default) directly over the track, the exact sunken/default surface pairing cards already use for 'raised above the page'. pillRadius (8px) = trackRadius (12px) − trackPadding (4px) — concentric corners, not a coincidence: an inset shape needs a proportionally smaller radius to look correctly nested inside its parent's rounded corner. trackPadding doubles as the gap between adjacent pills — tight by design, they're meant to read as one contained control, unlike underline's own (looser) inter-tab gap.

hover.$description: fill.neutralHover — one step darker than the track itself (surface.sunken/gray.100 → gray.200), same 'darker on hover so it stays visible' rule used everywhere else this session.

underline.$description: No background at rest, plain text — the active tab is marked only by a 2px bottom bar (a literal in the generated CSS, not itself a scale value worth tokenizing — one visual step bolder than the 1px baseline it overlaps). A 1px baseline (border.default) spans the full tab list, matching how the current live product's own underline-style tabs use a full-width hairline; the active indicator sits directly over it. Hover DOES get a background (fill.neutralHover, the same token segmented's hover already uses) — text-color-only hover was tried first and found too subtle to notice; a light background pill on hover while keeping the colored bar exclusive to the active tab is the common pattern (GitHub, Notion, Linear all do this).
